summary: Explains a risk score: each signal that fired becomes a bar starting where the running total left off, and a total row shows the final score after clamping to 0–100. It appears in the event drawer, the Simulation Center and the Lab, builds its markup with the escaping `html` template from dom.js, and cascades the rows in with an anime.js timeline from motion.js.

notes.text: Header comment: each signal's weight moves a running total, and the last row shows the clamped final score, the visual answer to 'why did this score X?'.

Imports `html` (escaping template), `levelOf` and `raw` (marks a string as already-safe HTML) from dom.js; `animate`, `motionEnabled`, `set` and `timeline` from motion.js; and `mitre`, which renders a badge linking to a MITRE ATT&CK technique.

Each contribution has a `signal` name, a `weight` (negative weights lower the risk), a `detail` sentence and an optional MITRE technique, ordered heaviest first with negatives last. `total` is the engine's final score, and `showDetail: false` hides the detail lines (the Lab does this).
`running` accumulates the sum of weights down the list.
For each contribution, `start` is the running total before it is added.

Adds the weight and returns a copy of the contribution with its `start` and `end`. Weights 40, 25 and −10 become 0→40, 40→65 and 65→55: each bar begins where the previous one ended, which is what makes it a waterfall.

The axis range: `lo` is the lowest point any step reaches (never above 0) and `hi` the highest (never below 100), so the track always spans at least 0–100 and stretches when the raw sum runs past 100 or below 0 before clamping.
`pct(v)` is a linear scale from that range to 0–100%, used for each bar's CSS `left` and `width`.
The final score: the engine's `total` when given (`??` only falls back on `null` or `undefined`, so a genuine 0 is kept), otherwise the raw sum clamped into 0–100, the same rule the engine applies.
`clamped` is true when the raw sum differs from the final score (weights summing to 130 give a score of 100), so the total row can say so.
Builds one row per step; `negative` marks risk-reducing signals.
Each bar spans from the lower of `start` and `end` to the higher, so a negative step reaches back left from the previous total; a minimum width of 0.6% keeps tiny steps visible.

Positive bars take the colour of the level the running total has reached at that step, so the bars change colour as the sum crosses 30, 60 and 80. Negative bars always use the LOW slate, and charts.css gives them a hatched pattern.
The row's label column: the signal name in bold and, when enabled and present, its detail sentence in small text.
The track, with the bar placed absolutely by percentage `left` and `width`; the `lvl-` class sets its colour and `neg` switches to the hatched style.

The weight column: a `+` before positive weights (negative ones already carry their minus sign), then, if the signal maps to an ATT&CK technique, a space (wrapped in `raw`) and its MITRE badge. Closes the row.
Closes the map over the steps.
The level of the final score, used to colour the total row.
Renders the chart; when no signals fired, an empty-state message says the event matches the customer's baseline. `String(...)` turns the safe-HTML object into a plain string for `innerHTML`.
The total row: the label 'Risk score' with a note reading either `sum N, clamped to 0–100` or `sum of weights`.
The total bar runs from 0 (`pct(0)`, which is not the left edge when the range dips below zero) to the final score, followed by the final number in the final level's colour.
Closes the total row and the wrapper.
With motion off, the finished chart is simply left as rendered: content is never hidden waiting for an animation.
Pre-hides what the timeline will reveal: rows turn transparent and bars are flattened to `scaleX: 0`, instantly (`set` applies values without animating).
An anime.js timeline schedules several animations on one clock; every step defaults to the `outExpo` ease.

For each signal row, fades and slides it in from 8 px to the left (380 ms), then grows its bar (620 ms) starting 300 ms before that fade ends. The position `i ? "-=260" : 0` starts the first row at time 0 and every later row 260 ms before the timeline's current end, so rows cascade with overlap; charts.css sets `transform-origin` so positive bars grow from the left and negative ones from the right.
Then the total row fades in and its bar grows over 900 ms, each overlapping the step before by 200 ms.
The final-number element, and a `{ v }` object for anime.js to tween.

Counts the number up from 0 to the final score. Its delay grows by 140 ms per row so the count lands roughly as the total bar grows, and each frame writes the rounded value; the closing brace ends `waterfall`.
